stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 0 < c < 9 \), for which \( f(c) = -8 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: No. Every tabulated value of f is greater than -8, so the Intermediate Value Theorem does not apply on \( [0, 9] \).

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous on \( [0, 9] \).
Every tabulated value of f is greater than -8, so no two of them have -8 between them.

The Intermediate Value Theorem needs -8 to lie between two values of f, so it guarantees nothing here, and a differentiable f with these values can stay greater than -8 throughout. So no such c must exist.

options.label: Yes. Since f is differentiable, it is continuous on \( [0, 9] \), so the Intermediate Value Theorem gives at least one such c.
options.derivation: the theorem applied with the straddling inequality never checked
